text.text_excerpt: Growing up, I rarely got the chance to eat meat. For the longest time I thought bacon was fried baloney. Hot dogs were the closest thing I ever had to sausages. And steak? The closest I ever came to that dream was a hamburger. At the time I had no idea as to what I was missing. I will always remember the first time I ate ribs. It was the high point of my tenure in undergrad. I was sitting at on the edge of my chair with both elbows propped up on the wooden table, clutching the riblet like a fat kid on mardi gras. I just recently moved to New Orleans and I've been looking for some good BBQ food. I work at Baptist hospital and this place came up. I decided to head here after work and give it a try. When I walked in, I was struggling to decide what to order on their huge wall menu so the owner greeted me and told me to try their lunch special which included a main, a side, a salad and beans over rice for 6 dollars (7 for ribs). I decided to go for the ribs with mashed potatoes and corn bread. I couldn't believe I could get ribs here this cheap! I'm from California where BBQ ribs normally cost 15-20 dollars an order. Warning: it smells like heaven in there. As if the smells don't entice you enough, they then give you these HUGE portions at great prices. Today I ordered their lunch special- a seafood baked potato. Chockful of crawfish, shrimp and imitation crab, the potato was perfectly seasoned and had the right amount of cheese to complement the rich meal. It was big enough for me to make two meals out of it. In addition, I was impressed with their service. Because the potato was going to take 15 mins, they gave me a free coffee.
